actions: assists elbow extension, stabilizes elbow (dynamically tensions the joint capsule)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Small triangular muscle continuous with triceps' medial head; active throughout elbow extension to protect the joint capsule from impingement.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

trigger_points.location_description: In the muscle belly just distal and posterior to the lateral epicondyle, between the epicondyle and the olecranon
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: A small, focal pattern over the lateral epicondyle
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Forceful extension and pronation; associated trigger points in triceps (especially medial head), supinator, and wrist extensors
trigger_points.notes: Produces lateral epicondylar pain resistant to extensor-origin treatment; case reports describe an 'anconeus syndrome' of lateral elbow pain relieved by treating the muscle; differentiate from pain referred into this region from triceps TrP1/TrP2, supinator, brachioradialis, ECRL/ECRB, extensor digitorum, supraspinatus, posterolateral plica, radial head pathology, or posterolateral rotatory instability
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded elbow muscle reference document (Simons DG, Travell JG, Simons LS. Travell & Simons' Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction, vol. 1, 2nd ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1999: ch. 32, Anconeus, with triceps brachii)
